title: Web-push armed by a stray tap in all three bundles; only the tenant copy cannot be turned off
why: Three rows, two files, two code sites: `S-264` and `S-760` cite overlapping line ranges inside the same `app-tenant.html` push block (22704-22735 and 22712-22744) under two different channels, `pwa` and `web-push`, while `S-761` is a separate block in `maya-os-site/index.html`. The defect has two halves and they are not localized the same way. The ask is missing everywhere: the same auto-arm — a one-shot `pointerdown` listener that fires `Notification.requestPermission()` on the user's next tap anywhere in the document — sits in `app-tenant.html` (:22745), in `app.html` (:40736) and in the MAYA OS bundle (:37565), so no bundle asks inside the product before the browser asks. The off switch is missing in one: `S-264`'s row records `__meUnsubscribePush`, `AWebPushControls` and `ANotifyCard` at zero hits in `app-tenant.html`, and `S-760` records its registration as fire-and-forget with no server receipt — the optimistic-success pattern a notification control is forbidden to use. The MAYA OS copy is what its row actually says it is: live and correctly server-receipt-confirmed, with `unsubscribe` in its capability list — correct on receipt and revocation, not on consent. It sits in this group because one control implemented three times — `app.html`, `app-tenant.html`, `maya-os-site/index.html` — is the duplication the chat-first rebuild exists to end. The proposal is to collapse them onto one `notifications` capability that asks first, in the conversation, and records the answer: that fixes the tenant bundle's missing off switch and the prompt-by-tap in all three, but the two halves do not carry the same urgency.
disappear: The tap-triggered permission prompt, in every bundle that carries it. The silent auto-subscribe in `app-tenant.html` — one code site, described twice in this group as `S-264` and `S-760` — goes with it, together with the fire-and-forget registration that never confirms a server receipt. The MAYA OS block `S-761` also goes, but only as a duplicate: it folds into the unified `notifications` capability after the merged bundle proves parity for MAYA OS tenants, not as part of the fix. The `app.html` copy is not a row in this group, so its retirement is not what is being signed here — but it carries the identical auto-arm, so its users see the same change in behaviour when the capability lands.
remain: Push itself, as something the user turned on and can turn off: one `notifications` capability owning `Notification.requestPermission`, `pushManager.subscribe`, server-receipt confirmation and unsubscribe — the capability set `S-761` already has and `S-264` lacks. The MAYA OS block stays in place and working until that successor is proven; nothing is removed from a live tenant first. Parity here is measured as whether a tenant user can disable push, not as whether push still works — that is what `S-264`'s own row requires. The server keeps the last word on which devices are actually registered: the registration endpoint already refuses devices it will not accept, and today the tenant bundle's fire-and-forget call discards that refusal, so a device can hold a browser-level subscription the server never registered. The successor has to show that answer instead of swallowing it. None of these three rows is a primary-nav entry, so the primary-nav collapse moves nothing with this group.
risk: MEDIUM — the two halves carry opposite risks and must not be sequenced as one step. Leaving `app-tenant.html` as it stands keeps tenant users on a subscription they cannot turn off from anywhere in the UI, and leaves every bundle firing the OS prompt off a stray tap, so there the risk is in not acting; the merge is cheap to implement, but only if it ships the controls and not merely the runtime. Retiring the MAYA OS block early is a real regression — its row states that doing so "removes a working notification control from a live tenant" — and it depends on unresolved decision D10, which this group does not close. Nothing retires on signature: all three rows are marked not retirable, with parity and authority still red. `S-760` carries liveStatus UNKNOWN, so nothing here may be approved on the premise that the tenant push path works today. Not HIGH: no authority or tenant-isolation boundary moves, and signing changes no deployed byte.
user_impact: Anyone signed into the tenant bundle (`сайт и приложение/app-tenant.html`) has the browser's OS notification prompt fired by the next tap anywhere in the document — once a session is detected, `__meMaybePush` arms a one-shot `pointerdown` listener (app-tenant.html:22745) that calls `Notification.requestPermission()` — and if they allow it the device is subscribed with no screen in that bundle to turn it off again. Verified: `__meUnsubscribePush`, `AWebPushControls`, `ANotifyCard`, `push_unsubscribe`, plus `me_web_push_disabled` and `me_web_push_episode_id`, all return 0 hits in that file. Scope caveat the original dropped: S-760 records this push block as liveStatus UNKNOWN because HTML-bundle deployment could not be established read-only, so this is what the bundle does when served, not a measured population. Correction to the framing: app.html:40736 and maya-os-site/index.html:37565 carry the byte-identical auto-arm block, so their users are auto-prompted by a stray tap too — the group's headline defect is not localized to the tenant bundle. What those two bundles have that the tenant bundle lacks is revocation, not an ask: all four symbols plus an «Отключить устройство» button (app.html:16388) and the `me_web_push_disabled` flag that stops the auto path re-subscribing after an opt-out. So after the merge a tenant user gains both the ask and the off switch, while an app.html / MAYA OS user gains the ask — what they notice is that the prompt stops being fired by a tap, not that controls appear. All of this is contingent, not delivered: retirement is gated on parity measured as "can a tenant user disable push" rather than "does push still work", S-761 depends on unresolved decision D10, the one-bundle endpoint is measured at Gate 10 and not enforced, and signing K1 changes no deployed byte.
security_impact: No authority or tenant-isolation change — but the original's stated mechanism is wrong, and that matters because it is the sentence licensing "NONE". `window.__meAuthReq` is not a server-side gate: at app-tenant.html:22381-22392 it is a client-side credential builder that returns null only when localStorage holds no Telegram initData, no `tg_auth_data` and no `web_session_token`. The real gate is server-side and narrower than the bundles' own comments claim: `push_subscribe_handler` (webhook_server.py:8440) is "verified Client registration only", carries no owner/master branch, and refuses with `verified_client_push_required`; `channel_proof` (legacy_client_command_bridge.py:13-27) accepts only Telegram initData, Telegram widget `auth_data` or a Maya JWT, so the `X-Session-Token` / `session_token` web channel that `authReq` will happily send is rejected outright; the legacy `_push_db` store is gone and only `/api/push/subscribe` and `/api/push/unsubscribe` are registered. The conclusion still holds — the client never decides the role, `Notification.permission` is a browser-OS gate that was never an authority check, nothing load-bearing is removed and no new server-side authority check is required — with one tightening: the recorded answer is itself new server-side state, so "nothing server-side has to replace it" is true of the authority check, not of the record. The audit gain is real and stronger than "minor": app-tenant's fire-and-forget `fetch(...).catch(function(){})` at :22729 swallows exactly the 409 a web-session-only tenant user will receive, so that device can hold a live browser-level push subscription the server refused to register — a structural divergence, not a hypothetical one, which the receipt-confirmed `__mePushCall` closes. The revocation gain is bounded: `__meUnsubscribePush` refuses without a locally stored `me_web_push_episode_id`, so the off switch is per-device and depends on that localStorage entry surviving.
